# Decisions

One entry per decision: what was decided, on whose word or which source, and the date.
A value without an entry here is a draft.

## Confirmed by Ilja

| # | Decision | Word, date |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | This repository holds the system only: principles, colours, rules, elements. No application screens. Later projects take from it. | 2026-11-19 |
| D2 | `tokens.json` is the source. The build writes CSS, and every element carries an HTML reference. A Swift generator comes later. | 2026-11-19 |
| D3 | Mobile first. The desktop layout is derived from the mobile one, never the other way round. | 2026-11-19 |
| D4 | ARC Mk.1 is the starting point, not the target. The target is a modern cyber system: Cyberpunk 2077 and Edgerunners primary, Iron Man secondary. | 2026-11-19 |
| D5 | Artefacts in English, the reply to Ilja in Russian. | 2026-11-19 |
| D6 | Cyan leads. Yellow marks attention, red marks alarm. | 2026-11-19 |
| D7 | Barlow Semi Condensed is the UI face; JetBrains Mono keeps the voice of machine data. | 2026-11-19 |
| D8 | Motion stays one-shot: a sweep, a glitch, a reveal and a caret, each on an event, never on a timer. | 2026-11-19 |
| D9 | A product may own a categorical palette; the accent and the status colours stay system. | 2026-11-19 |
| D10 | A category is carried by its word and its position; a tint marks at most two categories that pass the check, never as the only cue. | 2026-11-19 |
| D11 | The attention colour is a ladder of three steps from Ilja's own RAL palette: `#D9A62C` for text, `#CB8E1E` for a fill, `#A87300` for a pressed control. | 2026-11-19 |
| D12 | Critical means stop now: the system is under threat or data is at risk. Its hue is raspberry, 333°, from RAL 4010 Telemagenta: `#D65A92` for text, `#BC4077` for a fill. | 2026-11-19 |
| D13 | The ok green is NVIDIA's `#76B900` with `#4F7D00` as its fill, on Ilja's word after the measurement showed it passes every gate. | 2026-11-19 |
| D14 | Critical is blood raspberry at 348°: `#E15671` for text, `#B8213F` for a fill. | 2026-11-19 |
| D15 | Critical is raw magenta-violet at 308°: `#ED23D2` for text, `#AE0E99` for a fill. | 2026-11-19 |
| D16 | A glow marks the top step of a ramp, at intensity `v3`: halo 4 px at 30 %, glyph shadow 3 px. | 2026-11-19 |
| D17 | The light scheme ships: paper ground, deep values, one value per status, ink flipped to paper on fills, and no level glow. | 2026-11-19 |
| D18 | The icon set is a catalogue, not a hand-drawn list: take the glyphs you need from it. | Ilja, 2026-11-20 |
| D19 | The system ships as a release pack: a version in the dictionary, a changelog and an archive. | Ilja, 2026-11-21 |
| D20 | The pack ships a filter: a project markup and stylesheet are checked against the dictionary, and the run either passes or fails. | Ilja, 2026-11-21 |
| D21 | The outside check is a step of the release, not a lucky accident: unpack the pack, let a model that has never seen the system build two screens from it, then run the filter and the audit on what it wrote. | Ilja, 2026-11-21 |

## Decided by evidence

| # | Decision | Reason and source |
|---|---|---|
| E1 | Spacing, type and radius scale from fluid units (`--arc-u`, `--arc-fs`) derived with `clamp()` from the container inline size. Percentages carry inline shares only. | A percentage on `padding-top`/`padding-bottom` resolves against the containing block's inline size, so vertical padding cannot be a height fraction. MDN `padding`; CSS 2.1 §8.4. `--arc-u` is 16.00 px at a 390 px container, measured. |
| E2 | Shell edges use `env(safe-area-inset-*)` and `100svh`. | `viewport-fit=cover` plus insets is the documented mechanism; `100vh` overflows when browser chrome is present. MDN `env()`. |
| E3 | A filled accent carries near-black text, never white. | Measured: white on cyan 1.77:1, on yellow 1.30:1. Near-black on the same fills is 11.33:1 and 15.41:1 — `tools/contrast.py`. |
| E4 | The palette is measured by tool, not asserted in prose. | Mk.1 stated ratios that were close but never computed; one shipped pair fails AA outright. 18 pairs in `tokens.json` are gated now. |
| E5 | Animate `transform` and `opacity` only. A pulsing glow is an opacity change on a separate layer. | An animated `text-shadow` or `filter` re-rasterizes the region each frame; 390×844 at DPR 3 is 2.96M device px per frame. `research/engineering-limits.md` §1.6, §2. |
| E6 | Keep the three-layer architecture (ambient, content, control) and the base-8 grid from Mk.1. | Both are load-bearing in film craft and in Apple's control-layer rule; neither conflicts with the cyber grammar. `research/film-hud-and-trends.md` §3. |
| E7 | Drop the HUD screen-curvature shader and the ambient motifs (arc-reactor pulse, data rain). | A curvature warp needs an SVG filter, canvas or WebGL and is imperceptible at 390 px; the motifs are costume, not craft. `research/cyberpunk-grammar.md` §2.4. |
| E8 | The "80% film aesthetic / 20% usability" ratio of Mk.1 is retired. | It encoded "mostly pretty, some usable". Usability is the baseline; the intensity comes from the game grammar. `research/film-hud-and-trends.md` §3. |
| E9 | The hairline sits at `rgba(0, 212, 255, 0.48)`, not at 0.30. | At 0.30 the line measures 1.96:1 on the base ground; a component boundary needs 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11). At 0.48 it measures 3.27:1. |
| E10 | No control is shorter than 44 px, so there is no S size. | The first build shipped a 36 px button; the frame audit named it. A touch target is a physical constraint, not a density step. |
| E11 | A value is measured through the DevTools protocol at an exact frame. | Headless Chrome with `--window-size` left the layout viewport at 500×644 while the pixels said 390×844 — the readout was measured on the wrong page. `tools/shot.mjs` forces the size and prints the numbers. |
| E12 | Two alarm classes, never two in one view: `critical` (magenta) for a security event or an intrusion, `error` (red) for a failed operation or a negative value, `attention` (yellow) for a value that drifts. | The game mixes ornament and feedback into one red and reads as "too much red" (`research/cyberpunk-grammar.md` §1.2). A panel carries its class in its brackets and one top rule, never in a second border colour. |
| E13 | Zero radius everywhere. A fill is chamfered on two opposite corners; a frame is a hairline plus brackets; the chamfer lives on a pseudo-element, so the element keeps an uncut focus ring. Inputs keep a full rectangular frame. | `research/cyberpunk-grammar.md` §2.1–2.2; a `clip-path` cuts the outline at the notch, so the ring cannot sit on a clipped element (WCAG 2.4.13). |
| E14 | Fonts ship as WOFF2 with their SIL OFL text under `assets/fonts`. | No font service at run time; a reusable system does not depend on a third party. Barlow Semi Condensed 400–600, JetBrains Mono as one variable file. 124 KB in total. |
| E15 | Rajdhani is out, although it is the face of the game itself. | Rendered on the same frame, its 12 px uppercase labels read thinner than Barlow Semi Condensed, and Chakra Petch wraps the 11 px label onto two lines. Evidence: `docs/compare-typefaces.png`. A face is one token, so this is reversible. |
| E16 | The hairline is neutral `#44697C`, not cyan. | At 0.48 alpha the cyan line met 3:1 and read as a selected state on every panel — the pilot screen had no way to show which card mattered. The neutral measures 3.27:1 on base and 3.01:1 on a panel. |
| E17 | Panel corners are neutral by default; `--active` takes the accent. | Same cause: a view with six cyan brackets has no accent economy left. |
| E18 | A root screen uses `.arc-shell--app`: fixed head, one scroll container, a bar outside it. | The pilot put the bottom bar in the flow and it fell below the fold; the audit could not see a missing bar. |
| E19 | A dialog is a native `<dialog>`, styled. | The focus trap, Escape and the top layer are platform behaviour. Re-implementing them is the defect the control layer was meant to prevent. |
| E20 | The frame audit flags a clip only when `overflow-y` is hidden or clip. | The first predicate flagged `.arc-screen` for scrolling 1178 px inside 695 px — a legal scroll container. A gate with a false positive gets switched off. |
| E21 | A tab keeps the 44 px floor in both axes, so a short label owns a 44 px width. | The audit named `arc-tabs__tab 44.0px` on width after the height was already correct. Same floor as E10, second axis. |
| E22 | The skeleton sweep animates one gradient with `transform`, never the bar. | A shimmer that moves a `background-position` repaints the bar on every frame; the gradient layer costs one composite. |
| E23 | Every animation lives inside one `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` block. | Measured through the DevTools protocol with the media feature forced to `reduce`: all four effects report `animation-name: none`. A shortened animation is not the same as none. |
| E24 | Numeric columns take a fixed width (`--arc-table-col`), never `auto`. | The first table set each row as its own grid with `auto` columns, so the head and every row sized to their own content. Measured after the fix: all four rows report the same column right edges, 205.5 / 281.3 / 357.2 px. |
| E25 | A switch is a 44 px control around a 24 px track. | A 24 px painted track is the right picture; a 24 px hit target is not. The floor applies to what the finger meets, not to what the eye reads. |
| E26 | A code block scrolls sideways and never wraps **by default**. | On the pilot's detail screen a wrapped log record read as two records. `white-space: pre` plus horizontal scroll keeps one record on one line. Amended 2026-11-20 by the wrap act on Ilja's word: the default stands, and a reader may press `WRAP` for the record — scroll 462 px inside 356, wrapped 356 with nothing hidden. The wrapped form carries no indent, because `text-indent` indents the first line of the block and not of each record: a 48 px hanging indent put the second record's timestamp at the continuation position. |
| E27 | A selected chip is filled with the accent; selection outranks status. | With an outline-only accent, the yellow `FAILED` chip looked more chosen than the active filter `MUSIC`. |
| E28 | The frame audit compares every element's edges with the viewport, not only `scrollWidth`. | `.arc-shell` sets `overflow-x: clip`, so a button that left the frame produced no scrollbar and no finding. Positive control: a 500 px box is now reported as `right 516.0 / 390`. |
| E29 | A control that insets a child draws its own edge as an inset ring, never as a border. | The switch measured 3.95 px of knob inset on the leading edge against 1.96 px on the trailing one: a 1 px border per side, twice. As a ring the four insets read 3.96 / 3.96 / 3.96 / 3.95. |
| E30 | A category colour must clear 3:1 on the ground and stand 40° from every system hue; a category is carried by label and position first. | `tools/categories.py` on GRND's live pair: 3 of 4 hues fail (21° from the accent, 17° from attention, 1° from ok). With five system hues at 40° clearance only two narrow bands remain, so four hue-coded categories cannot pass at all. |
| E31 | The readout is 3.5 × the type unit — 56 px at a 390 px frame — in tabular mono at zero tracking. | A timer is the one number a screen is about, and the type scale stopped at 40 px. Measured on the pilot: `01:23` occupies 168 px at 56 px, which leaves room for a unit and still reads at arm's length. Proportional figures and tracking would shift the line on every tick. |
| E32 | An icon is one `em` of 2-unit stroke in `currentColor`; the sprite ships as a file and the page needs an HTTP origin. | `getBBox` measured 0 × 0 on all nine icons over `file://` and 4–12 units over `http://127.0.0.1`. A blank icon row looks like a tidy row, so the frame audit now reports a zero-box icon: nine findings on the file render, none on the served one. |
| E33 | Bars carry area only; a value needs a labelled axis and a line chart needs SVG. | Measured bar heights 25.3 / 44.3 / 63.3 / 53.8 / 34.8 px and equal widths 58.5 px — the reader compares, and cannot read a number. |
| E34 | The fluorescent attention `#F3E600` is retired for honey, and status colours ship as steps. | The fluorescent hue measured 14.82:1 with saturation 1.00 and read as a siren on a dark instrument panel. Ilja's ladder measures 8.68 / 6.83 / 4.70 on the base ground, ink on the fill 7.09, and keeps a factor of 1.9 above the text threshold. His own inverse `#8A6100` measures 3.48:1 and stays out of the dark scheme. |
| E35 | The ink on a fill follows the fill's luminance: near-black above, white below. Every status therefore ships a text step and a fill step, each measured. | Ilja's `#237F52` and `#BF3922` measure 3.89:1 and 3.51:1 as text but 4.97:1 and 5.49:1 under white; `#EE9E93` is the mirror at 9.14:1 as text and 2.11:1 under white. One rule replaces a per-colour decision. |
| E36 | The green text step is derived at Ilja's own hue: `#3FBC7C`, 7.99:1. | Leaf Green `#237F52` cannot carry text on the dark ground, and the palette has no lighter green. `#3FBC7C` holds the 151° of RAL 6032 and lifts lightness until it passes. Flagged as derived, not as his colour. |
| E37 | The critical class moved from neon magenta to raspberry and gained a fill step. | Text `#D65A92` measures 5.27:1, the RAL 4010 fill `#BC4077` 3.80:1 with white at 5.07:1 and near-black at 5.48:1 on the light step. RAL-to-hex is unofficial: published tables give 4010 as `#BB4077`, `#BC4077`, `#C05281` and `#C63678`. `#BC4077` is pinned; a print or film job verifies against a physical fan. |
| E38 | Saturation is raised in relative steps: +15 % for attention and critical, +30 % for error, at unchanged hue and lightness. | Error text `#EE9E93` → `#FC9485` (9.14 → 8.93), fill `#BF3922` → `#D7280A` (3.51 → 3.86); attention `#D9A62C` → `#E6AB1F` (8.68 → 9.38), fill `#CB8E1E` → `#D89211` (6.83 → 7.39); critical `#D65A92` → `#DF5191` (5.27 → 5.26), fill `#BC4077` → `#C53776` (3.80 → 3.84). Measured fact worth keeping: a saturation step barely moves contrast — under 0.4 in every pair — so it buys colour without buying or losing legibility. All 28 pairs still pass. |
| E39 | Honey gains another 10 % of saturation, and the pale error text is replaced by a deeper coral. | Text `#F0AF15` (9.97:1) and fill `#E29507` (7.84:1) for attention; error text `#F05A3F` at 5.73:1 replaces `#FC9485` at 8.93:1, which Ilja read as thin — the palest step of a hue is what reads washed out, and saturation alone cannot fix it because a hand keeps lightness and buys saturation. Critical text `#DF5191` and both dark fills `#C53776`, `#D7280A` are taken as they stood. All 28 pairs pass; the shallowest text margin in the set is now 1.06× (critical, 5.26:1). |
| E40 | The green is derived at saturation 0.70 and its fill follows the same recipe, so Leaf Green leaves the system. | Text `#26D57B` measures 10.00:1 with near-black ink at 10.40:1; the fill `#17824B` is the same hue and saturation at lower lightness, 3.98:1 with white at 4.85:1. NVIDIA's `#76B900` was measured and rejected: hue 82 sits 48° from the honey attention, so two status classes would read as two shades of one signal, and the colour is a vendor brand. His RAL 6032 `#237F52` measured 3.89:1 as text and sat at saturation 0.50 beside a palette that now runs 0.70–1.00. |
| E41 | The derived green is replaced by the vendor green, and the earlier objection is downgraded from evidence to taste. | `#76B900` measures 8.00:1 as text, 8.32:1 under near-black, and its fill `#4F7D00` 3.92:1 with white at 4.92:1 — every gate passes, and the 40° rule too at 48° from the honey attention. The two objections (same warm family, a vendor brand) are judgments the gates do not measure, and Ilja chose the colour. Recorded so a later session does not "fix" it back on the strength of E40. |
| E42 | The critical hue moved 15° towards red because the raspberry read as sweet. | Text `#E15671` measures 5.30:1, the fill `#B8213F` 3.06:1 with white at 6.31:1 and near-black on the text step 5.51:1. Sweetness comes from lightness in the pink range, not from saturation, so hue and lightness moved and saturation stayed. Two warnings recorded: the fill sits 2 % above the 3:1 a boundary needs, and the hue is 21° from error — the smallest separation in the set, which Rule 3 covers only because the two classes never share a view. |
| E43 | The critical hue moved from blood to magenta-violet, and the separation problem disappears with it. | Text `#ED23D2` 5.30:1, fill `#AE0E99` 3.05:1 with white at 6.32:1 and near-black on the text step 5.51:1. The hue now stands 61° from error and 94° from attention, so the three alarm classes separate by hue alone; E42's warning about a 21° gap no longer applies. The fill still sits 2 % above the 3:1 floor, which is the recipe, not an accident. |
| E44 | The glow is a level signal, and its intensity came from a rendered ladder, not from a number picked in the abstract. | Five intensities on one screen, then `liked`, `v1`–`v3` and `none` on a zoomed crop; Ilja took `v3`. Measured against its own family: `liked` is 7 px at 70 %, `mid` 7 px at 60 % with two wider glyph shadows — the difference is the glyph shadow, and that is what makes a number look soft. Also measured: the rendered screens differ by up to 202 levels in a channel, so a "they look identical" reading is a scale artefact, not a duplicate. |
| E45 | The light scheme was derived from Ilja's own palette and gated on its own ground. | Text `#12161A` 16.56:1 on `#F7F4EE`; accent `#0A6E7E` 5.40; attention `#8A6100` 5.05; ok `#1A6642` 6.33; error `#BF3922` 4.56; critical `#A0108A` 6.52. The gate now measures 45 pairs across both schemes, 0 below the ratio. Two defects the render caught: a dark teal fill with dark ink measured 3.25:1, so the light scheme's ink flipped to paper; and a disabled control at opacity 0.4 was unreadable on paper, so the floor is 0.55. The thinnest margin in the set is error on paper at 4.56:1 — 1.01x. |
| E46 | The ambient grid is a per-scheme token, and the light ground carries it at half strength. | On paper the grid at the dark scheme's 55 % read as millimetre paper and competed with the content. It is now 0.28 with an 18 % hairline, an effective 5 % ink. The token lets a scheme tune the texture without touching a single element. |
| E47 | A render pins its scheme, because an unparameterised render is the light scheme. | Headless Chrome answers `prefers-color-scheme: light`: `docs/screenshot.png` and `docs/screenshot-light.png` were byte identical (`f9c8700…` at both) while the README captioned the first as the dark scheme. `tools/shot.mjs --scheme dark\|light` now emulates the media feature and sets the page flag; the two files differ, and the body ground reads `rgb(5, 8, 13)` against `rgb(242, 239, 233)`. The audit runs once per scheme, both clean. |
| E48 | A link keeps the 44 px floor inside a sentence, and a step indicator carries its number in words and its position in shape. | An action in words is still met by a finger: the link measures 110.05 × 44 px inside a sentence and 44 × 44 px at its shortest, with `vertical-align: middle` so the paragraph keeps one baseline at 44 px. The step track would otherwise separate its steps by two greys, so the label reads `STEP 2 OF 3 · DEVICE` and the current segment stands 7.91 px against 3.95 px. Segments measure 105.48 / 105.50 / 105.48 px — equal, so the position reads from the whole row and not from one wide bar. |
| E49 | The touch-target predicate covers every control, and exempts only an anchor that runs inside a sentence. | It read `button, .arc-input` alone, so a 20 px link passed the gate silently — a `.arc-link` in a flex parent reports `display: flex` and would never have been measured either. It now reads `button, a[href], input, select, textarea, [role="button"]` plus the input class and skips only `a[href]` with `display: inline` (WCAG 2.5.8 inline exception). Positive control: a 20 px anchor reported as `A 20.0px`, a plain sentence link reported nothing, and all eight pilot screens and both schemes stayed clean. |
| E50 | A line chart is SVG generated from the numbers, stretched without distorting its strokes, with its axis in HTML. | A hand-written path is a coordinate typed by a person and wrong at the first data change, so `tools/chart.py` emits it from a 100 × 100 viewBox. Measured on the render: the plot is 287.66 × 120 px, the three gridlines sit 60 px apart, and the computed stroke stays 2 px for the line and 6 px for the marker at 390 px and at 900 px because every mark carries `vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke`; the marker is a zero-length round-capped segment, so it paints as a round dot where a `<circle>` in a stretched viewBox would paint an ellipse. The axis numbers are HTML in a two-column grid, so a wide frame adds width and never enlarges the caption, and each number is lifted half its height to sit on its gridline. The series is gated at 3:1 on the ground in both schemes — 10.90:1 dark, 5.40:1 paper — taking the gate to 47 pairs. |
| E51 | A render and an audit disable the browser cache for the session. | With a reused profile directory headless Chrome served the previous page after an edit: a chart that had just been added was invisible to `querySelectorAll('.arc-chart')` — `figures: 0`, `sections: 1` — while `curl` fetched the file that carried twelve `arc-chart` classes. `Network.setCacheDisabled` on the session fixed it: the same URL then reported `chart: 1`, and every audit and every committed frame was re-run afterwards. A measurement on a stale page is not evidence. |
| E52 | A glyph enters the set because a screen asks for it, and a word never shares its 44 px row. | Seven glyphs arrived with named acts — `eye` and `eye-off` (show/hide), `copy` (the record's bar), `link` (reset), `trash` (remove), `refresh` (retry, re-run), `chevron-left` (back) — taking the sprite from thirteen to twenty, and each name comes from the screen that asked for it rather than from a catalogue. The field's action moved from the word to the mark: the word plus the mark needs 72 px inside a row that reserves 71.87 px, so the word leaves and the mark carries `aria-label` and `aria-pressed` at the body size — act 44 × 44, icon 16 × 16, glyph bbox 13.3 × 8. `tools/icons.py` runs inside the gate: a naive number scan read `l-6 6` as a stray -6 and reported thirteen legal glyphs as broken, so the checker walks the path and measures where each step lands; a control point at y = 30 fails it, and all twenty pass. |
| E53 | A typed mark is a defect, and the set was checked once against five public libraries. | All twenty earlier glyphs exist in Carbon (2779), Tabler (5491), Lucide (2410), Feather (287) and Material Symbols (2122), several under another name (`subtract`, `text--wrap`, `view--off`, `player-pause`), so the vocabulary is standard and the gaps are ours. Coverage across the libraries cannot rank a gap: 59 of the 76 concepts tested against them sit in all five, brands and text formatting included. The screens ranked instead, and eight glyphs arrived — `chevron-up` (the pair of a shipped glyph), `alert-circle` and `check-circle` (the field message typed `✗` on two screens), `settings`, `bell`, `clock` (the timer and the meta line), `calendar`, `user` — taking the sprite to 28, all inside the grid. Two typed marks remain in the screens and move to the sprite: the item's `›` and the field's `✗`, because a character follows the font and the platform fallback while a mark follows the grid. |
| E54 | The catalogue is Lucide 1.77.0 under the ISC licence, and the sprite is built from a manifest. | 2410 glyphs vendored in `assets/icons/` (1.16 MB of svg, one file each, 24-unit grid, 2-unit stroke); `assets/icons-manifest.json` names the 28 the product ships and `tools/icons_sprite.py` turns exactly those into `assets/icons.svg` (4822 bytes) — all 2410 in one file would be twelve times the stylesheet. Six names were adopted with the set (`x`, `triangle-alert`, `circle-alert`, `circle-check`, `refresh-cw`, `text-wrap`) rather than aliased, so one drawing answers to one name. Caps and joins moved to `round`: the set is drawn for them, and a miter join grows a spike at 16 px. The catalogue page carries 2410 inline glyphs in 701 KB; the first full render at DPR 3 was roughly 157 megapixels and timed out, so the committed artefact is DPR 1 at 1280 × 12535. Two glyphs, `letter-i` and `tally-1`, drew a zero-width box and the audit called them broken — it now reports a missing icon only when both axes are empty. |
| E55 | A choice from many is a sheet built on a native dialog, and the system now owns the scrim and the lift as tokens. | Compared with six systems — @material/web (23 components), Carbon (130), Polaris (121), Primer (74), Spectrum (90), Ant Design (79) — the 59 concepts tested leave three gaps that all six carry (checkbox, radio, action menu) and five that four or five carry (select, combobox, slider, badge, listbox); the sheet is the structural one, because on a phone it hosts the select and the action menu that a desktop system draws as a dropdown. Measured at 390 × 844: the sheet is 356.4 px tall and starts at 487.6, six options at 44 px each, the select control 324.4 × 44. The dialog hard-coded its shadow and its backdrop, so both became tokens (`--arc-shadow-panel`, `--arc-shadow-sheet`, `--arc-overlay-scrim`, 0.45 on paper against 0.72 on the dark ground). Two audit findings were false positives of the icon predicate: an icon inside a closed dialog has no layout box, so a hidden icon is skipped now; a single vertical stroke has no width, so only a box empty in both axes counts. |
| E56 | A choice row is a native input stretched over the whole row, and a menu on a phone is the sheet its trigger opens. | Measured at 390 × 844: the row is 324.4 × 44 and the input that receives the press fills all of it, so the audit and the finger agree on the target; the mark is 23.7 px inside it and is painted on a sibling because a background image cannot follow `currentColor`. A chosen box is the accent fill with the invert ink and a check; a chosen radio is a 2 px accent ring with a 45 % dot, so the two are told apart by shape, not by hue. The menu reuses §8.26: four rows at 44 px, the last one `--danger` in the error hue with its trash mark. The first version stretched the input to the mark only and the audit reported four targets at 23.7 px — the failure was the model, not the tolerance: the picture was the hit area. |
| E57 | The radio dot is a radial gradient, because a flex-centred percentage box drifts on fractional geometry. | Ilja saw the dot off its centre on a zoomed render. Measured on the pixels: the previous build put the dot 0.50 px up and left of the ring at a 768 px container, where the mark is 26.89 px and the dot 12.00 px; at 390 px both forms measure 0.00. Eighteen combinations of six widths (320, 360, 390, 414, 430, 768) and three densities: the gradient form is 0.00 in all eighteen, the flex form is −0.50 at 768 in all three. The cause is a percentage box centred by flex inside a mark that is not a whole number of pixels. |
| E58 | A range box is the target with the track inside it, a badge is not a target, and a combobox list hangs off its field. | Measured at 390 × 844: the slider input stands at 44 px with the track 4 px inside, after the first cut sized the box to the thumb and the audit reported a 23.7 px target; the fill is one gradient driven by `--arc-slider-value`, because Chrome has no progress pseudo-element, and the number beside it is written by the same handler (62 % → 80 % on input). The badge stands at `--arc-space-5` and carries no floor, because the bar item or the bell under it is the target. The combobox list joins the field with no gap and no top rule, so the two read as one control; its height caps at eleven units and it scrolls. The badge first sat flush against its word; it now carries the gap itself — the word is consumer text and cannot — measured 7.91 px, with the box 0.69 px above the lowercase x-height centre. |
| E59 | A disabled fill is a ground with low ink, not a faded accent; the form summary stands above the action. | A primary button at 55 % opacity still reads as the action — the fill is the loudest thing on the screen and a faded one still says "press me". It now takes `bg.raised` with `fg.low`, measured 4.33 on the dark ground and 5.41 on paper, and the gate holds the pair at 3:1 because a disabled control is exempt from 4.5 yet still has to be read. The form summary measures 324.4 × 141.9 px with two rows of 44 px, 15.8 px above the buttons, and it lists only the fields that fail now: the first version kept a static row for a field that had passed, which sends the reader to a field that is fine. |
| E60 | A group of choices carries a legend, and a limit is counted rather than truncated. | GOV.UK (39 components) and USWDS (50) both ship a fieldset and a character count, and neither closes the gap by `maxlength`. Measured on the showcase: 38 element selectors in §8, all rendered; the count line sits under the field at the micro step in tabular mono and flips to the error ink when the value passes the limit — 120 in the demo, 95 left on load, over by 3 after a paste of 123. The fieldset resets border, margin and padding so the rows keep their own rhythm, and the legend takes the field label's type rather than a heading step. Ilja then saw the textarea's text sitting on its frame: measured, inset 0 at the top against 11.87 at the side — a single-line input centres itself in the row, a textarea does not. `padding-block: var(--arc-space-2)` puts the ink 14 px from the top against 13 px from the left. |
| E61 | A full-page capture drops its density to fit one texture, because a taller capture paints a blank band. | A page of 8003 px at DPR 3 is 24009 device pixels; the seam fell at 5650 px and everything after it was blank — the bottom of a panel and the character count under its field vanished from `docs/elements.png` while the live page showed them (verified on a probe page and by computed style). `--full` now lowers the scale until height × density fits under 16 000 and prints the density it used: the sheet is 390 × 9623 at 1× at 2.1.0, and the count band carries ink again (767 pixels where it had none). |
| E62 | A success screen carries the record of what it made, and a task list states each step in words. | GOV.UK ships a panel and a task list as separate components and neither exists in the six systems compared earlier, so the pair arrived from the government sets. The result mirrors `.arc-fault`: the same shell, the same centring, one class word, plus a record block (device, key) because "done" without the thing is a claim. The task rows measure at the control height with the state in words at the trailing edge — `Done`, `In progress`, `Not started` — so the state survives the loss of colour; every row is a link, since a finished step is changed as often as an open one. |
| E63 | The last four gaps from the government sets are a note, a warning, a fold and an affix. | Of 81 names in GOV.UK (39) and USWDS (50), 45 were already covered and 25 refused with a reason (web chrome, no hover on touch, a native control that does better, marketing); the remaining eight reduce to four concepts. The fold is a native `<details>` so the keyboard and the no-JS state stay the platform's, and its mark turns with `transform` only. The affix sits in the flow inside the control's frame instead of forcing a padding computed from a glyph width. The note is a rule and a ground, never a frame, because a frame says "this is the object". The warning carries a triangle before it carries a hue. |
| E65 | The pack is 31 files and 219 KB (2.1.0), and it gates itself in a clean directory. | "python3 tools/package.py" writes dist/arc-2.1.0.tgz with sorted names, mtime 0 on every entry and mtime 0 in the gzip header, so the same tree builds the same bytes — two consecutive runs print one sha256 (the plain `tarfile.open(..., \"w:gz\")` stamped the header with the wall clock and two runs on one tree carried two digests); the 2410-file icon catalogue stays behind because a consumer rebuilds and measures, not re-derives. Extracted into an empty directory the pack runs its own gate: 49 pairs, 0 below the ratio, "assets/icons.svg is the shipped sprite — 31 glyphs match the manifest (no catalogue in this pack)", 31 glyphs within the grid, 44 elements rendered, "markup: 44 element instances current", and the frame audit of its own index.html is clean. index.html ships for that reason: the page is the reference a project copies its markup from, and the surface check needs it. The sprite and the geometry check tolerate a catalogue-less tree with a printed note instead of failing. |
| E66 | Every element seals the properties it must not inherit, and a filter decides whether a project consumes the system. | Measured in a hostile parent — line-height 3, a serif face, 4 px tracking, lowercase, centred — the chip line-height went 19 to 39 px and its face went serif, the key/value value took the tracking and the casing, while the button stayed identical because it declared its stack. The seal declares nine inherited properties on 56 element roots and all three probed elements now match their clean instance to the pixel. tools/lint.py applies four rules — no raw value in a consumer CSS, no selector naming an .arc- class, no arc- class the system does not define, no value typed into an inline style — and on its first run it found five raw values in the pilot, all inside a dead holes block duplicating shipped elements. The system own showcase failed it too, with one arc- prefixed class of its own; both read clean now, 12 pilot files and 1 showcase page against 229 system classes. |
| E67 | The canon carries an appendix generated from the page: one instance of every §8 root with its child classes, and the gate fails when the block and `index.html` disagree. | §8 described an anatomy in prose, so a consumer agent pulled the classes out of `index.html` by eye and reported `arc-item` without `__text`/`__title`/`__meta`/`__end`, `arc-codeblock` as a variant instead of a wrapper, and `arc-readout` as one span. `tools/markup.py` takes the first instance of each root, strips attributes to `class` (plus `type`, `role` and a `<use>` `href`), writes text as `…` and stops at five levels; 44 instances, 676 lines. Positive control: renaming one child class in the page failed `--check` with exit 1, and the regenerated block is byte-identical on a second run. |
| E68 | The audit compares `aria-expanded` with the panel it names, and a control marked disabled must not answer a click; both are proven with a live control. | The toast was not a CSS defect but a drift between the state in the markup and the state on the screen, and no frame shows it. The showcase reports `ariaExpandedChecked: 3`, `disabledControlsChecked: 2`, both schemes clean; on a page of deliberate defects the audit reports five findings — an expander that says true over a hidden panel, one that says false over a painted panel, one that names no panel, an anchor with `aria-disabled`, a `div` with `role=button` and a listener, and an anchor carrying `disabled` — while the truthful expander, the truthful collapser and the native disabled button stay silent. The counter probes one enabled control first and reports `enabled answers, disabled silent`, because a predicate that never fires prints what a clean page prints. |
| E69 | A row that carries a phrase is an `.arc-item`: the phrase is the title, its evidence the mono meta, the control at the end. `.arc-kv` keeps pairs. | The key of `kv` is set in caps with tracking and §4 cuts a label at two words, so «Alert when a disk passes 85 %» set that way is the least readable line on the screen — and in a table cell it turns a column into a paragraph. Measured on the showcase: the phrase takes 212 px in a 212 px slot at the h3 step and reads in full, its row stands at 62.3 px beside the rows above it, and the switch keeps its 44 px box in `__end`. Recorded with a refusal, because `.arc-item__title` is `nowrap` with an ellipsis: a phrase that outgrows the row is a sentence for the body text, not a longer title. |
| E70 | The chip's ground moved to `bg.base`, because the gate measures that ground and did not measure `bg.raised`. | The outside check on 2.1.0 measured the ink the chip actually paints on: dark critical 4.22:1, light attention 4.37:1 and light error 3.95:1 on `bg.raised` — three pairs under 4.5 while `contrast.py` printed 49 pairs and 0 below, because the element's own fill was outside the declared set. `bg.base` is declared for all five status inks in both schemes; the lowest is light error at 4.56:1. No colour changed, so Ilja's palette stands: the element moved onto a measured ground, exactly as E59 moved the disabled control onto `bg.raised`. |
| E71 | `.arc-table__scroll` gives its row one column per cell (`grid-auto-flow: column`, `grid-auto-columns: var(--arc-table-col)`), and a table row carries no state class. | The pack's own four-column demo was broken: with the fixed three-column template the fourth cell fell onto a second implicit row, and the row measured 69.27 px against 35 for its neighbours. With one column per cell all four cells share a top and the right edges agree at 129.6 / 205.5 / 281.3 / 357.2 px inside a 324.4 px row, so the container scrolls as §8.11 promised. A state on a row is refused rather than added: one coloured row in a grid reads as a zebra stripe, and the state goes into the panel head as a chip that names it in words. |
| E72 | Layout geometry is a gate of its own: `tools/geometry.mjs` with a declared contract, not a sweep. | Every gate this system had judged values, states and the frame, and none judged placement: a 20 px top inset beside a 16 px step, a panel with no inner padding beside one with 16.23, and GRND's own screens with controls at 26, 32 and 38 px all passed the frame audit. The first cut swept every element and printed 45 findings on this page, of which 39 were legal — a centred stack, a control sized to its content, a half step, a bleed section — so the tool now checks only the relations a page declares in `tokens/geometry.json`: inset, centre, columns, rows and rhythm (a padding or gap is a step, a stroke, a half step, or the sum of two). Measured: the showcase reports 0 findings in both schemes, and a planted 7 px padding is reported as `paddingLeft 7.00px is not a step`. |

## Open forks

Each fork blocks a value. The recommendation is the evidence-based default; Ilja's word overrides it.

| # | Fork | Recommendation | Why it is open |
|---|---|---|---|
| F2 | Dark only, or a light scheme as well? | Dark only in Mk.2; add a scheme later if a project needs it. | A light cyber scheme is a second design problem: neon on white breaks every measured pair. |
